_about: The test-links page (test-links.html) reads this list: Karl's change list. `checks` is the Features to check section at the top: one item per new feature (id, name, build, one link, numbered steps, what you should see), written from the real code and walked through with tests/features/walk.mjs before a build is called finished; the ticks live only in Karl's browser, and an item stays here until Karl has ticked it. The rest of the page: Live = on the site for everyone. Testing = behind a flag, waiting for Karl to keep or retire it. Retired = deleted. Every build adds or updates its entries (CLAUDE.md, Working with Karl). Each entry is a name, one plain sentence (`about`) and, for Live and Testing, its buttons. A button's `query` is the part after the address: card, level, seed, flags, sign-in skipped. `level` in a link is the saved level number (Add to both sides and Divide it: link level 2 is shown as Level 1). `reset: true` clears this browser's progress first; `look` is one sentence on what to look for; `notLive` says plainly why a link won't work on the live site.

checks.name: Add, combine, fraction on 3x + 4 = 19
steps: Click the button. It opens the new Two-step equations card, Level 1, on 3x + 4 = 19.
Click Add (the top box in the panel on the right), type −4 and press Enter. The 4s cross out and a new row reads 3x = 19 − 4.
Drag the 19 onto the 4 beside it. A box opens under them: type 15 and press Enter. The row reads 3x = 15.
Click Multiply (the second box in the panel). Three options open beside it: click the second one (▢ over ▢), type 1/3 and press Enter. The new row reads x = ⅓(15).
Click the box after x =, type 5 and press Enter. Drag the 5 onto the x in 3x + 4 = 19, then press Enter three times.
checks.see: After Add the right side stays 19 − 4 until you put it together: nothing is worked out for you. The check reads 3x + 4 = 19, then 3 × 5 + 4 = 19 under it, down to 19 = 19 and Balanced.

checks.name: Add at 3x = 15: the three x boxes message
steps: Click the button. It opens Two-step equations, Level 1, on 3x + 4 = 19.
Click Add (the top box in the panel on the right), type −4 and press Enter.
Drag the 19 onto the 4 beside it. A box opens under them: type 15 and press Enter.
Click Add (the top box in the panel on the right), type −3 and press Enter (trying to cancel the 3 in 3x).
Read the message, then click Undo.
checks.see: The 3x is outlined and the message says “3x is three x boxes, not a 3 to cancel. Adding −3 does not take them away. To get one x, take a fraction of the three x boxes: ⅓.” After Undo, Multiply’s options are open with the fraction lit and previewed, and the hint says “one of the 3 x boxes is ⅓”.

checks.name: The fraction is greyed until each side is one term
steps: Click the button. It opens Two-step equations, Level 1, on 3x + 4 = 19.
Click Multiply (the second box in the panel), then click the second option (▢ over ▢).
Click Add (the top box in the panel on the right), type −4 and press Enter. Click Multiply and the second option again.
Drag the 19 onto the 4 beside it. A box opens under them: type 15 and press Enter. Click Multiply and the second option once more.
checks.see: The first two times it says “That move works once each side is one term.” and nothing opens. Once the row is 3x = 15, the fraction blank opens under the equation.

checks.name: Level 3: Trade places first, with the symmetric-property line
steps: Click the button. It opens Two-step equations, Level 3, on 19 = 4 + 3x.
Read the pop-up beside the panel and look at the Trade places box (the fourth one).
Click Trade places.
checks.see: The pop-up ends “This is the symmetric property: if a = b, then b = a.” and Trade places has a blue ring. After the click the new row reads 4 + 3x = 19.

checks.name: b − ax = c with Flip everything: 4 − 3x = −11
steps: Click the button. It opens Two-step equations, Level 5, on 4 − 3x = −11.
Click Add (the top box in the panel on the right), type −4 and press Enter.
Drag the −11 onto the 4 beside it. A box opens under them: type −15 and press Enter. The row reads −3x = −15.
Click Flip everything (the third box in the panel), then the green Go.
Click Multiply (the second box in the panel). Three options open beside it: click the second one (▢ over ▢), type 1/3 and press Enter.
Click the box after x =, type 5 and press Enter. Press Enter again (from Level 3 a right answer is checked in one short line).
checks.see: After the flip a pop-up says “Multiplying both sides by −1 flips every sign. −x becomes x.” and the row reads 3x = 15. The check starts 4 − 3x = −11 with 4 − 3 × 5 = −11 under it, then Balanced.

checks.name: Flip everything: the first flip says what −1 does (once)
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 1, on −x = 12.
Click Flip everything (the third box in the panel), then the green Go.
Click the box after x =, type −12 and press Enter. Drag the −12 onto the x, press Enter twice, then click Next problem.
On the next equation, click Flip everything, then Go.
checks.see: The first flip shows a small pop-up: “Multiplying both sides by −1 flips every sign. −x becomes x.” The flip on the second problem works the same way but shows no pop-up.

checks.name: Finished old Two-step levels already count on the new card

link.label: Open the old Two-step card · Level 1

steps: Click the button. It opens the old Two-step equations card (now off the home screen), Level 1. Click Skip tour if a tour starts.
Type 6 and press Enter, then press Enter again for the next problem. Do the same with 8, 1, 3 and 2.
Click ← Packs at the top left, then Solve it.
checks.see: The old card says Level 1 is complete. On the home screen the new Two-step equations card shows Level 1 done and Level 2 open. (On a student’s own device, any old Two-step level they finished shows the same way, on the level of the same kind.)

checks.name: Level 1 (ax + b = c): a right guess makes the next problem a move
steps: Click the button. It opens Two-step equations, Level 1, on 3x + 4 = 19.
Click the box after x =, type 5 and press Enter. Drag the 5 onto the x, then press Enter three times.
Click Next problem.
checks.see: The first problem ends “Yes! x = 5, and it balances.” The second problem, 5x + 8 = 18, opens with “Your mental math is very strong. Let’s try solving this next problem using a move first.” and Add has a steady ring.

checks.name: Level 2 (ax − b = c): 3x − 4 = 11
steps: Click the button. It opens Two-step equations, Level 2, on 3x − 4 = 11.
Click Add (the top box in the panel on the right), type 4 and press Enter.
Drag the −11 onto the 4 beside it. A box opens under them: type 15 and press Enter.
Click Multiply (the second box in the panel). Three options open beside it: click the second one (▢ over ▢), type 1/3 and press Enter.
Click the box after x =, type 5 and press Enter. Drag the 5 onto the x, then press Enter three times.
checks.see: Adding 4 gives 3x = 11 + 4, then 3x = 15 and x = ⅓(15). The check reads 3 × 5 − 4 = 11 down to 11 = 11 and Balanced.

checks.name: Level 3 (x on the right): Add first is fine too
steps: Click the button. It opens Two-step equations, Level 3, on 19 = 4 + 3x.
Click Add (the top box in the panel on the right), type −4 and press Enter (instead of Trade places).
Hover over the top dot beside Add in the panel.
checks.see: The new row reads 19 − 4 = 3x with no red message, and the dot opens to “Fewer terms” with a green tick.

checks.name: Level 4 (b + ax = c): 4 + 3x = 19, with the short check
steps: Click the button. It opens Two-step equations, Level 4, on 4 + 3x = 19.
Click Add (the top box in the panel on the right), type −4 and press Enter.
Drag the 19 onto the 4 beside it. A box opens under them: type 15 and press Enter.
Click Multiply (the second box in the panel). Three options open beside it: click the second one (▢ over ▢), type 1/3 and press Enter.
Click the box after x =, type 5 and press Enter. Press Enter again (from Level 3 a right answer is checked in one short line).
checks.see: Adding −4 gives 3x = 19 − 4 (the x term stays second until the 4s cancel). From this level the check is short: 4 + 3 × 5 = 19, then Balanced.

checks.name: Level 5 (b − ax = c): I’m stuck gives a reminder only
steps: Click the button. It opens Two-step equations, Level 5, on 4 − 3x = −11.
Click I’m stuck (bottom right).
Click I’m stuck again.
checks.see: Each time the 4 is outlined, the Add box is open under the equation, and the pop-up says “Look at the +4 next to x. What would we add to both sides to eliminate it? Type it in the box.” No balance, counters or Teach me.

checks.name: Level 6 (negative answers): 3x + 4 = −11
steps: Click the button. It opens Two-step equations, Level 6, on 3x + 4 = −11.
Click Add (the top box in the panel on the right), type −4 and press Enter.
Drag the −11 onto the 4 beside it. A box opens under them: type −15 and press Enter.
Click Multiply (the second box in the panel). Three options open beside it: click the second one (▢ over ▢), type 1/3 and press Enter.
Click the box after x =, type −5 and press Enter. Press Enter again (from Level 3 a right answer is checked in one short line).
checks.see: The rows read 3x = −11 − 4, then 3x = −15 and x = ⅓(−15). The check reads 3 × (−5) + 4 = −11, then Balanced.

checks.name: Level 7 (all mixed): 19 = 4 − 3x, finished with −⅓
steps: Click the button. It opens Two-step equations, Level 7, on 19 = 4 − 3x.
Click Trade places (the fourth box in the panel).
Click Add (the top box in the panel on the right), type −4 and press Enter.
Drag the 19 onto the 4 beside it. A box opens under them: type 15 and press Enter. The row reads −3x = 15.
Click Multiply (the second box in the panel). Three options open beside it: click the second one (▢ over ▢), type −1/3 and press Enter.
Click the box after x =, type −5 and press Enter. Press Enter again (from Level 3 a right answer is checked in one short line).
checks.see: Taking −⅓ of both sides finishes in one move: x = −⅓(15). The check reads 19 = 4 − 3 × (−5), then Balanced.

checks.name: Play it like a student: Two-step
steps: Click the button. It opens Two-step equations, Level 1, on 3x + 4 = 19. You are going to play a student who gets things wrong.
Mistake 1, ignoring the screen: touch nothing for 10 seconds. A good response is a gentle flashing of I’m stuck, with nothing else changing.

Mistake 2, skipping the fraction: click the box after x =, type 15 and press Enter. Drag the 15 onto the x, press Enter three times and wait two seconds. A good response works out 3 × 15 + 4 = 19 to 49 = 19, says the equation is not balanced, and leaves only Undo. Press Undo: the hint outlines the 4 and asks what to add to both sides. Click Got it.

Mistake 3, a move that makes it worse: the Add box is still open under the equation, so type 4 and press Enter. A good response lights the 4 and the 4 that was added, says they did not eliminate the term, and leaves only Undo. Press Undo, then Got it.
Mistake 4, a move at the wrong moment: click Multiply and the second option (▢ over ▢). A good response is a small note, “That move works once each side is one term.”, and nothing locked.

Mistake 5, a wrong sum: the Add box is open again, so type −4 and press Enter. Drag the 19 onto the 4, type 23 and press Enter. A good response says “19 − 4 is not 23. Press Undo and try again.” with the two numbers still readable. Press Undo: the hint lights 19 and −4 and says to drag one onto the other.
checks.see: Every mistake gets a calm answer in the real numbers, Undo is the way out of each error, and the hint after Undo points at the next move. Nothing is ever worked out for you.

checks.name: Level 1 (−x = b): only Flip everything is needed; the other moves say why not
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 1, on −x = 12.
Click Add (the top box in the panel on the right).
Click Multiply (the second box). Three options open beside it: click the first one (▢ × ( )), then the second (▢ over ▢).
checks.see: Add says “That move unlocks on a later card.” In the Multiply options the whole number says the same, the fraction says “That move unlocks on a later level.”, and only −1 × ( ) is live.

checks.name: Level 2 (b = −x): flip first, and x stays on the right
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 2, on 12 = −x.
Click Got it if a pop-up is open, then click the Flip button (the third box in the panel on the right, −x → x) and the green Go.
Type −12 and press Enter. Drag the −12 onto the x and press Next twice.
checks.see: The flip writes −1 × (12) = −1 × (−x), then −(12) = x, with x still on the right (that is fine). The check ends ✓ Balanced.

checks.name: Level 3 (−ax = b): flip, then take a fraction
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 3, on −3x = 12.
Click the Flip button (the third box in the panel on the right, −x → x) and Go. Then click the green Next.
Click Multiply, then the fraction option (▢ over ▢). Type 1, /, 3 and click Go.
Type −4, press Enter, drag it onto the x and press Next twice.
checks.see: After the flip the equation is 3x = −12 (No opposite box turns green). Taking ⅓ writes x = ⅓(−12), which is not worked out for you. The check ends ✓ Balanced.

checks.name: Level 4 (all four forms): a fraction first, then the flip
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 4, on 12 = −3x.
Click Multiply, then the fraction option. Type 1, /, 3 and click Go.
Click the green Next. Then click the Flip button (the third box in the panel on the right, −x → x) and Go.
Type −4, press Enter, drag it onto the x and press Next twice.
checks.see: Taking ⅓ first gives 4 = −x, with no red light (either order is fine). The flip then gives −(4) = x. The check ends ✓ Balanced.

checks.name: Level 5 (bigger numbers)
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 5, on −3x = 36.
Click the Flip button (the third box in the panel on the right, −x → x) and Go, then Next. Click Multiply, the fraction option, type 1, /, 3 and click Go.
Type −12, press Enter, drag it onto the x and press Next twice.
checks.see: 3x = −36, then x = ⅓(−36). The check ends ✓ Balanced.

checks.name: A helpful flip: −x = 12 becomes x = −(12)
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 1, on −x = 12.
Point at the Flip button (the third box in the panel on the right, −x → x) without clicking: a grey preview appears under the equation.
Click it, then click the green Go.
checks.see: The preview is −1 × (−x) = −1 × (12). After Go it is written in, then x = −(12): the 12 is not turned into −12 for you. No opposite box and Solved for x turn green.

checks.name: A flip that makes it worse: the spotlight, Undo, then the hint
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 3, on −3x = 12.
Click the Flip button (the third box in the panel on the right, −x → x) and Go, then the green Next. The equation is 3x = −12.
Click the Flip button and Go again, then wait two seconds.
Press Undo.
checks.see: −3x = 12 comes back with −3x framed in red (“x has a minus”) and “Flipping 3x = −12 made −3x = 12: now x has a minus. Press Undo.” Only Undo works. After Undo: “To get one x, take a fraction of both sides: one of the 3 x boxes is ⅓.” with the fraction option lit.

checks.name: −3x = 12 times −⅓ in one move is accepted
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 3, on −3x = 12.
Click Multiply, then the fraction option. Type −1 (the minus key, then 1), /, 3 and click Go.
Type −4, press Enter, drag it onto the x and press Next twice.
checks.see: It writes −⅓(−3x) = −⅓(12), then x = −⅓(12), with No opposite box and Solved for x green and no red. The check ends ✓ Balanced.

checks.name: Typed 12 for −x = 12: the hint points at Flip everything
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 1, on −x = 12.
Click the box after x =, type 12 and press Enter. Drag the 12 onto the x.
Press Next twice and wait two seconds. Press Undo.
checks.see: The check shows −(12) = 12, then −12 = 12, and says it is not balanced. After Undo: “−x = 12 means the opposite of x is 12, so x is not 12. Flip everything: multiply both sides by −1.” with the Flip button ringed and its preview under the equation.

checks.name: Trade places on 12 = −x, with the symmetric property
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 2, on 12 = −x.
Read the pop-up beside the panel.
Click Trade places (the bottom box in the panel). Then click the Flip button (the third box in the panel on the right, −x → x) and Go.
Type −12, press Enter, drag it onto the x and press Next twice.
checks.see: The pop-up says x is on the right, to click Trade places, and “This is the symmetric property: if a = b, then b = a.” Trading writes −x = 12; the flip gives x = −(12); the check ends ✓ Balanced. (Flipping first also works.)

checks.name: The check shows −(−12)
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 1, on −x = 12.
Click the Flip button (the third box in the panel on the right, −x → x) and Go.
Type −12, press Enter and drag it onto the x.
Press Next twice.
checks.see: The check starts with −x = 12 and, under it, −(−12) = 12, the blue (−12) right under the blue x. Then 12 = 12 and ✓ Balanced.

checks.name: After a correct first guess, the next problem needs a move
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 1, on −x = 12.
Without making a move, type −12, press Enter, drag it onto the x and press Next twice.
Click Next problem.
checks.see: The next problem (−x = 3) opens with “Your mental math is very strong. Let’s try solving this next problem using a move first.”, the Flip button ringed, and x = greyed until a move is made.

checks.name: Play it like a student: Flip everything
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 3, on −3x = 12. You are going to play a student who gets things wrong.
Mistake 1, ignoring the screen: touch nothing for 10 seconds. A good response is a gentle flashing of I’m stuck, and nothing else changing.

Mistake 2, dropping the signs: click the box after x =, type 12 and press Enter. Drag it onto the x, press Next twice and wait two seconds. A good response shows −3 × 12 = 12 turn into −36 = 12, says it is not balanced, and leaves only Undo. Press Undo: the hint says the minus belongs to x and lights the Flip button. Press Got it.

Mistake 3, a fraction that does not split: click Multiply, the fraction option, type 1, /, 2 and click Go. Wait two seconds. A good response says 3 boxes can’t make 2 equal groups and pulses Undo. Press Undo: the boxes, the counters and the fractions to choose from appear, ½ crossed off. Click ⅓.

Mistake 4, forgetting the sign at the end: the equation is now −x = 4. Type 4, press Enter, drag it onto the x, press Next twice and wait. Press Undo. A good response says −x = 4 means the opposite of x is 4, so x is not 4, and lights Flip everything.
Mistake 5, pressing I’m stuck again and again: press it twice. A good response repeats the reminder with the real numbers (this card has no pictures yet) and still leaves the move to you.
checks.see: Every mistake gets a short message built from the student’s own numbers, and there is always one clear thing to press next. Nothing gives the answer away.

checks.name: Picking up your number slides a faint copy of the equation into the check

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 3

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 3, on x + 8 = −4.
Click the box after x =, type −12 and press Enter.
Press and hold on the −12 and move it slowly toward the x, but do not let go yet.
Let go on an empty part of the page (not on the x).
Now drag the −12 onto the x in the equation and let go.
checks.see: While you hold the −12, a faint copy of x + 8 = −4 slides into the empty space on the right. Let go anywhere else and it slides back and nothing changes. Let go on the x and it stays there, solid, with (−12) + 8 = −4 written under it.

checks.name: The check writes the equation, then your number right under its x (Add to both sides)

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 3

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 3, on x + 8 = −4.
Click the box after x =, type −12 and press Enter. Drag the −12 onto the x.
Look at the first two lines on the right.
Press Next twice.
checks.see: The first line is x + 8 = −4 with a blue x; right under it is (−12) + 8 = −4, and the blue (−12) sits directly under the blue x. Next adds −4 = −4, then ✓ Balanced.

checks.name: The check writes the equation, then your number right under its x (Divide it)
steps: Click the button. It opens Divide it, Level 2, on 5x = −15.
Click the box after x =, type −3 and press Enter. Drag the −3 onto the x.
Look at the first two lines on the right.
Press Next twice.
checks.see: The first line is 5x = −15 with a blue x; right under it is 5 × (−3) = −15, and the blue (−3) sits directly under the blue x (the first line moves a little to the right to make room). Next adds −15 = −15, then ✓ Balanced.

checks.name: At big numbers, a battle asks who won first; the subtraction appears only after

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 5

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 5, on x − 2 = −15.
Click Add (the top box in the panel on the right), type 2 and press Enter. The equation is now x = −15 + 2.
Click I’m stuck, then click Battle!. One small box appears just under −15 and +2: Who won? −15 or 2?
Click the big + first, then the big −.
Type −13 and press Enter.
checks.see: At first there is only the one box (no greyed second box). The + gets “Not that one”. After the −, a second box appears to the right: “Subtract 15 − 2 to find how many of the −15 are left.”, and the first box still shows the − you picked. −15 and 2 stay bright; nothing is written in x = for you.

checks.name: At big numbers, a party asks for its sign first, then what to add

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 5

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 5, on x + 13 = −2.
Click Add (the top box in the panel on the right), type −13 and press Enter. The equation is now x = −2 − 13.
Click I’m stuck, then click Party!. One small box appears: A party of what? Pick the sign.
Click the big + first, then the big −.
Type −15 and press Enter.
checks.see: The + gets “Not that one. Look at the signs of −2 and −13.” After the −, a second box appears to the right: “Add 2 + 13 to find how many negatives.”, and the first box still shows the −. −2 and −13 stay bright; nothing is written in x = for you.

checks.name: A party of negatives typed without its sign gets a sign question

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 5

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 5, on x + 13 = −2.
Click Add, type −13 and press Enter. The equation is now x = −2 − 13.
Click the box after x =, type 15 (forgetting the sign) and press Enter. Drag the 15 onto the x, press Next twice and wait two seconds. Press Undo.
In the box at −2 and −13, click the big + first, then the big −.
Type −15, press Enter, drag it onto the x and press Next twice.
checks.see: After Undo, a box at the two numbers (both bright, the rest grey) says “−2 and −13 are both negatives. A party of negatives makes ___”. The + gets “Look again…” and the same question; the − says “Now type x, and keep the sign.” with x = bright. The −15 ends ✓ Balanced. (A wrong size, like −17, gets the usual hint instead.)

checks.name: A wrong sum keeps the two numbers lit

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 3

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 3, on x + 8 = −4.
Click Add (the top box in the panel on the right), type −8 and click Go. The equation is now x = −4 − 8.
Press and hold on the −4, drag it onto the −8 and let go. A box asks for their sum: type 5 and press Enter (a wrong sum on purpose).
Wait two seconds.
checks.see: The screen goes grey and a box says −4 − 8 is not 5, with Undo pulsing. The −4 and the −8 stay bright next to the box marked “check this”: they are what the question is about.

checks.name: A wrong answer keeps its reason lit, and your number is blue (Add to both sides)

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 3

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 3, on x + 8 = −4.

Click the box after x =, type −4 and press Enter. Drag the −4 onto the x in the equation. Two lines appear on the right: the equation itself, x + 8 = −4, and under it (−4) + 8 = −4, with the (−4) right under the x.
Press Next twice, then wait two seconds. The screen goes grey and a box says the equation is not balanced.
Look at the last line on the right, 4 = −4, and the words ✗ Not balanced under it.
checks.see: In the second line, the −4 you dropped in is the same blue as the x above it that it replaced. When the screen goes grey, the last line (4 = −4) and the words Not balanced stay bright and easy to read; Undo is the only button that works.

checks.name: A wrong answer keeps its reason lit, and your number is blue (Divide it)
steps: Click the button. It opens Divide it, Level 2, on 5x = −15.

Click the box after x =, type 4 and press Enter. Drag the 4 onto the x in the equation. Two lines appear on the right: the equation itself, 5x = −15, and under it 5 × 4 = −15, with the 4 right under the x.
Press Next twice, then wait two seconds. The screen goes grey and a box says the equation is not balanced.
Look at the last line on the right, 20 = −15, and the words ✗ Not balanced under it.
checks.see: In the second line, the 4 you dropped in is the same blue as the x above it that it replaced. When the screen goes grey, the last line (20 = −15) and the words Not balanced stay bright and easy to read; Undo is the only button that works.

checks.name: The faint number starts to move after 2½ seconds

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 3

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 3, on x + 8 = −4.
Click the box after x =, type −4 and press Enter. The −4 in the box now blinks: it is ready to be dragged.
Count slowly to three without touching anything.
Now drag the −4 onto the x in the equation.
checks.see: After about two and a half seconds a faint −4 slides from the x = box toward the x in the equation, and it keeps coming back until you drag the number yourself. Clicking the x does not put it in: only dragging does.

checks.name: At x = −3 + 5 the two numbers stay bright

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 2

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 2, on x + 5 = −3.
Click the top box in the panel on the right (+ ▢ = + ▢: that is Add). Type 5 and press Enter. The equation now has x alone: x = −3 + 5.
Click I’m stuck. A question floats above −3 and +5: Party or Battle?
Click Battle!
checks.see: The question goes away and says “Yes, a battle: the bigger team wins. Now type x.” The −3 and the +5 stay bright and easy to read, outlined, next to the x = box that is ready for you. Only the rest of the screen is grey.

checks.name: Dragging a term shows the same grey preview on both sides

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 1

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 1, on x + 8 = 11.
Press and hold on the +8 in the equation and drag it just to the left of the x. Do not let go.
Keep holding and drag it across the = onto the right side.
Drag it back to where it started and let go.
checks.see: Left of the x, a grey 8 sits in the place it would land, drawn in the equation itself (before, it was a dashed empty box). On the right side a grey −8 sits where it would land. Back where it started, the 8 shows grey in its own place, and nothing changes when you let go.

checks.name: Typing a slash turns Multiply into the fraction box
steps: Click the button. It opens Divide it, Level 2, on 5x = −15.
Click the Multiply box in the panel on the right (the second one down). Three choices open beside it. Click the first one, a single box × ( ).
Type 1, then press the / key (next to the right Shift on most keyboards), then type 5.
checks.see: When you press /, the single box turns into a fraction box: the 1 you typed becomes the top, the cursor jumps to the bottom, and the 5 makes ⅕ on both sides. The green button says Go.

checks.name: A fraction box can be retyped by tapping it
steps: Click the button. It opens Divide it, Level 2, on 5x = −15.
Click the Multiply box in the panel on the right. Click the second choice, the one with a bar between two boxes. Type 1, then 5. A small note under the fraction says “Tap a box to retype it.”
Click the top box of the fraction.
Click the bottom box of the fraction.
checks.see: Clicking the top box empties it and puts the blinking cursor in it. Clicking the bottom box empties that one too, and the cursor moves there. The other box keeps its number until you click it.

checks.name: Enter does the move, and never gives another clue

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 1

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 1, on x + 8 = 11.
Click I’m stuck once. A hint asks what to add to both sides, and a box is open for the number.
Type −8 and press Enter.
Press Enter again.
checks.see: The first Enter does the move: x + 8 − 8 = 11 − 8 appears, and x is alone. The second Enter does nothing. Before this change, Enter after I’m stuck gave the next clue and the second Enter wrote −8 over your own number.

checks.name: The counters at x = −3 + 5 no longer say “Nice drawing!”

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 2

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 2, on x + 5 = −3.
Click Add (the top box in the panel on the right), type 5 and press Enter. Click I’m stuck, then click I’m stuck again. The two numbers arrive as counters on the right.
Read the words under the counters.
checks.see: The words under the counters say “Party or Battle?”, with no “Nice drawing!”: you did not draw them, so the sentence no longer praises a drawing.

checks.name: The seesaw shows the check, line by line

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 3

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 3, on x + 8 = −4.
Click I’m stuck twice. The seesaw opens on the right. Type −8 and click Go. Click Battle!, then Next, then Party!.
Type −12 and press Enter. The seesaw now shows the original equation, x + 8 = −4, with an empty x box. Drag the −12 onto that x box.
Press Next, then Next again.
checks.see: When the −12 lands, the x box becomes 12 minus counters in a blue box with a small x above it, beside 8 plus counters, and the other side has 4 minus counters, each line written below it. After the next press, the left side is 4 minus counters and the beam is level. The last words are ✓ Balanced, and the seesaw says Balanced too. A check done beside the equation (without I’m stuck) is drawn as before.

checks.name: On the seesaw, a number over 12 is one labelled box

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 5

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 5, on x − 2 = −15.
Click I’m stuck twice. Type 2 and click Go. Click Battle!, then Next. Click Battle! again for −15 and 2.
Type −13 and press Enter. Drag the −13 onto the x box on the seesaw.
Press Next, then Next again.
checks.see: The x box turns into one box that says −13, with a small x above it (not thirteen counters), beside 2 plus counters; the other side is one box that says −15. The last line is balanced, and the beam is level.

checks.name: Add never gives an answer of 0, 1 or −1

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 2

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 2, on x − 3 = −1.
Click the top box in the panel on the right (the one that looks like + ▢ = + ▢: that is Add). Type 3 and press Enter.
Type 2 and press Enter five times. The next problem comes up.
Do the other four problems the same way: work out the answer in your head, click Add, type the number that cancels the one beside x, press Enter, type the answer, press Enter five times.
checks.see: The five problems are x − 3 = −1, x − 4 = 6, x − 6 = −9, x − 2 = 5 and x − 5 = −7, and their answers (2, 10, −3, 7, −2) are never 0, 1 or −1. The first one used to be x − 4 = −3, whose answer is 1; the −1 in the first problem is on the right side of the equation, and that is fine.

checks.name: The seesaw opens beside the work, never over it

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 1

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 1, on x + 8 = 11.
Click I’m stuck once (a hint asks what to add), then click I’m stuck a second time. The seesaw appears, with “Build the equation” above it.
Look at the screen: the equation is at the top left, the seesaw is on the right, and x = with the green button sits below both.
Now make your window act like a shorter laptop: hold Ctrl and press + twice (Command and + on a Mac). That zooms to 125%. Look again at the same things. Press Ctrl and 0 (Command and 0) to go back.
checks.see: At both heights the seesaw sits in the space to the right of the equation. Nothing is covered, and x = and the green button are still on the screen without scrolling.

checks.name: Divide it: the hint after Undo names the idea with the real numbers
steps: Click the button. It opens Divide it, Level 2, on 5x = −15.
Click the box after x =, type 4 and press Enter.
Drag the 4 from the x = box onto the x in the equation.
Press Next twice. Wait two seconds: the screen greys and says the equation is not balanced.
Press Undo (bottom left).
checks.see: The three Multiply options open with the fraction one (▢ over ▢) lit, and the message reads “To get one x, take a fraction of both sides: one of the 5 x boxes is ⅕.” The green button says Got it.

checks.name: After a wrong move on the seesaw, the picture shows what cancelled and what did not

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 3

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 3, on x + 8 = −4.
Click I’m stuck twice. The seesaw appears.
Type −3 (the minus key, then 3) and click the green Go.
It asks Party or Battle for 8 and −3. Click Battle!, then click the green Next.
It asks again, for −4 and −3. Click Party!
Wait two seconds.
Press Undo.
checks.see: After the wait the screen greys. On the seesaw the +8 and the −3 each show three pairs crossed off, with the 5 left over marked “still here”, the other side is lit, and the message reads “Battle! 8 and −3: 3 pairs cancel (crossed off), but 5 is still beside x. Press Undo.” Undo pulses with an arrow. After Undo, a hint points at the +8 and asks what to add.

checks.name: At x = −3 + 5: choose Party or Battle, cross off pairs, count, type x

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 2

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 2, on x − 5 = −3.
Click the top box in the panel on the right (Add). Type 5 and press Enter. The work now reads x = −3 + 5.
Click I’m stuck. It asks “−3 + 5: party or battle?” Click I’m stuck again. Counters appear on the right: three − under the −3 and five + under the 5, with Party! and Battle! under them. Click Battle!
Tap one − counter. It and one + counter get an orange line through them.
Tap an empty part inside the dotted box around the + counters (not on a counter). Every pair that can go is crossed off.
Count what is left, type it in x = (2) and press Enter.
checks.see: The crossed-off counters stay on the screen, with the lines through them, and two + counters are left. After you type 2 the check begins: “Let’s check that x = 2 is the solution.”

checks.name: Play it like a student: Add to both sides

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 3

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 3, on x + 8 = −4. You are going to play a student who gets things wrong.
Mistake 1, ignoring the screen: touch nothing for 10 seconds. A good response is a gentle flashing of I’m stuck, with nothing else changing and nothing taken away.

Mistake 2, a wrong answer from the start: click the box after x =, type −4 (copying the number on the right) and press Enter. Drag the −4 onto the x in the equation. Press Next twice and wait two seconds. A good response writes x + 8 = −4 with (−4) + 8 = −4 under it, turns that into 4 = −4, says the equation is not balanced, and leaves only Undo to press. Press Undo, then Got it.

Mistake 3, a move that makes it worse: type 8 (the box under the equation is open) and click the green Go. Wait two seconds. A good response marks the 16 “got bigger”, explains with your own numbers (+8 + +8 did not eliminate the term), and pulses Undo. Press Undo, then Got it.

Mistake 4, a move that only half cancels: type −5 and click Go. Wait two seconds. A good response marks the leftover 3 “still here” and says +8 was only partially canceled by the −5 you added. Press Undo, then Got it.

Mistake 5, pressing I’m stuck again and again: press it four times. A good response gives a bigger clue each time (look at the +8, then which number cancels it, then choose Add, then “−8 cancels the +8. Add it to both sides yourself.”) and still leaves the move to you.
checks.see: Every mistake gets a short message built from the student’s own numbers, and there is always one clear thing to press next. Nobody is left stuck, and nothing gives the answer away.

checks.name: Play it like a student: Divide it
steps: Click the button. It opens Divide it, Level 2, on 5x = −15. You are going to play a student who gets things wrong.
Mistake 1, ignoring the screen: touch nothing for 10 seconds. A good response is a gentle flashing of I’m stuck, with nothing else changing and nothing taken away.

Mistake 2, a wrong answer from the start: click the box after x =, type −15 (copying the number on the right) and press Enter. Drag the −15 onto the x. Press Next twice and wait two seconds. A good response writes 5x = −15 with 5 × (−15) = −15 under it, turns that into −75 = −15, says the equation is not balanced, and leaves only Undo to press. Press Undo, then Got it.

Mistake 3, a whole number that does not help: the three Multiply options are already open, so click the first one (▢ × ( )), type 5 and click the green Go. A good response says “5 × (5x) makes 25x: still not one x. Try a fraction.” in a small note, and nothing is locked.
Mistake 4, flipping the sign: click Multiply, click the −1 × ( ) option and click Go. A good response says the sign changes but there are still 5 x’s, and points to a fraction.

Mistake 5, a fraction that does not split: click Multiply, click the ▢ over ▢ option, type 1 and then 2, and click Go. Wait two seconds. A good response says it doesn’t split (5 boxes can’t make 2 equal groups, and −15 can’t be shared into 2 equal groups), and pulses Undo. Press Undo: it shows the five x boxes and the fractions to choose from. Press Got it.
Mistake 6, pressing I’m stuck: press it twice. A good response gives a bigger clue the second time (first the 5 boxes and 15 counters, then “take ⅕ of both sides”) and still leaves the move to you.
checks.see: Every mistake gets a short message built from the student’s own numbers, and there is always one clear thing to press next. Nobody is left stuck, and nothing gives the answer away.

items.name: Help gaps closed (Build F, Part 3)
items.about: Divide it’s hint after Undo lights the fraction option under Multiply. A wrong move on the seesaw gets a picture spotlight, then Undo, then the hint. At x = 11 + −8 the counters come drawn, and the student crosses off the pairs and counts.

links.label: Divide it · the hint after Undo
links.look: Type 4 in x =, press Check, drag the 4 in, press Next twice: not balanced. Press Undo: the Multiply options open with the fraction lit and its preview, and “one of the 5 x boxes is ⅕”.

links.label: A wrong move on the seesaw
links.look: Press I’m stuck twice, type −3, press Go, then Battle, Next, Party. The screen greys; the 8 and −3 on the seesaw show 3 pairs crossed off and 5 left (“still here”), the other side lit, Undo pulsing. Press Undo: the hint at the +8.

links.label: Cross off the pairs at x alone
links.look: Add −8 to both sides. Press I’m stuck, Battle, I’m stuck. The counters for 11 and −8 are drawn on the right: tap a counter (it and a − go), then tap a whole box (every pair goes). Crossed-off counters stay. Count the 3 left and type 3.

items.name: The seesaw beside the work (Build F, Part 2)
items.about: The seesaw, its tray and the counters at x alone now draw in the space on the right, beside the equation, and never cover the work. The page is wider on both Solve it cards, and x =, the green button and the corners stay in one place.

links.label: Level 1 · build the seesaw
links.look: Press I’m stuck twice. The seesaw appears on the right; x + 8 = 11 stays on the left. Build it, add −8, then type 3 and check: the check sits under the seesaw.

links.label: Level 3 · the seesaw rungs
links.look: Press I’m stuck three or four times (Model it, Choose the move, Guided). The seesaw is on the right each time; x =, Go and the corners don’t move.

links.label: Level 3 · counters at x alone
links.look: Add −8 to both sides, then press I’m stuck, Party, I’m stuck. The counters tray is on the right, its two boxes over −4 and (−8).

links.label: Level 5 · big numbers at x alone
links.look: x − 9 = −13: add 9, then press I’m stuck, Battle, I’m stuck. The Add or Subtract box is on the right, beside x = −13 + 9.

links.label: Divide it at the wider width
links.look: Same as before, on the wider page.

items.name: The seesaw (Build D-2, Part 5)
items.about: On the seesaw, Add has a box under each side: the number is typed once and its counters go onto both sides. Once built, “Choose a move” greys everything but the moves and the question. At the end, the value can be dragged onto the x on the balance or onto the equation under it. The big-number box is gone once the value is being checked. I’m stuck stays lit while the screen is greyed, wherever it has more help.

links.label: Build, choose, add
links.look: I’m stuck twice, build x + 8 = 11 on the balance: everything greys but the moves (and I’m stuck). Choose Add, type −8: counters on both sides. Go, then Battle twice, type 3, Check: drag the 3 onto the x on the balance.

links.label: Seesaw from the start
links.look: I’m stuck twice (the seesaw), choose Add and type −8 once: both sides get −8.

items.name: One Multiply button (Build D-2, Part 4)
items.about: Multiply opens three options beside it: a whole number, a fraction and −1. Hovering one previews it on the equation; clicking it makes it solid. The fraction takes one digit on top and one below (the cursor jumps), with “Enter a unit fraction, like ⅕ or ½.” for 66 or 55, or after a while with nothing done. No thick outline on the selected box: the blinking cursor shows it.

links.label: Divide it
links.look: Click Multiply: three options. Hover each. Pick ▢/▢: type 6, the cursor jumps down; type 6 again: the unit-fraction pop-up. Pick ▢ × ( ), type 3, Go: “3 × (5x) makes 15x: still not one x. Try a fraction.”

links.label: Distribute drill
links.look: At −2x = 2: Multiply, then −1 × ( ), then Go: both sides × (−1), then 2x = −2. A whole number works too (negatives allowed).

items.name: Dragging a term (Build D-2, Part 3)
items.about: While a term is dragged, the equation itself shows where it would land (no extra row); across the line it turns red and can go before or after the other terms; the line is thin and stops short of the =. In the Distribute drill every product is typed with its x, and Flip everything writes a × (−1) step.

links.label: Drag across the line
links.look: Drag the +8 over the line: −8 appears in red in the equation, before the 11; keep going right past the 11 and it moves after it. Let go a little above or below the line: it lands where it was shown.

links.label: Distribute drill
links.look: Tap the minus, drag −2 onto the parentheses, type −2 and Enter: “Type every piece, including the x.” Type −2x. At −2x = 2, Flip everything: a row −2x × (−1) = 2 × (−1), then 2x = −2.

items.name: x = and checking a value (Build D-2, Part 2)
items.about: x = has no blinking cursor until it is clicked; the check says what is being checked; the value is dragged onto x (a click on x does nothing), and after 4 seconds a faint copy of it travels to x to show how.

links.label: x = cursor
links.look: No blinking line at first. Click the box after x =: it gets a blue outline and blinks. Click anywhere else, or type: the blinking stops.

links.label: Check wording and the ghost
links.look: Type −8, Check: “Let’s check that x = −8 is the solution. Drag the −8 onto an x above.” Wait 4 seconds: a faint −8 floats from x = up to the x, again and again. Clicking the x does nothing; dragging works.

links.label: Divide it
links.look: The same on Divide it: no cursor until x = is clicked; type 4 and Check for the new words and the ghost.

items.name: Add to both sides on the shared loop (Build E)
items.about: Add now runs on the same engine as Divide it: one help ladder that reads the shape of the equation on screen, the same check beside the equation, the same Undo and Start over. What changed for students: after the move that leaves x alone there is no Next (the next thing is typing x); Start over is live as soon as anything has been done; a move that only partly helps waits for Undo, in the seesaw too; a move made in the seesaw is written into the work.

links.label: Level 1
links.look: x + a = b. Add −8 (or the right amount), Go: no Next, the green button says Check until x is typed; the line under the move is solid.

links.label: Level 2
links.look: x − a = b. Add the wrong number: the error pop-up, Undo, the hint. Start over is live once you have done anything.

links.label: Level 3
links.look: Both forms. I'm stuck four times: the reminder, the seesaw, the two-sided move, the amount filled in. A partly helping move on the seesaw now asks for Undo first.

links.label: Level 4
links.look: x on the right: Trade places is pointed out first, then the move.

links.label: Level 5
links.look: Bigger numbers: at x alone, I'm stuck twice brings Count it's big-number walk when a number is past 12.

links.label: Numbers only (See why it works)
links.look: The numbers-only level is unchanged.

links.label: Divide it, for comparison
links.look: Divide it was already on the shared loop; it now uses the same help registry and the same play adapter as Add. Nothing should look different.

links.label: Class sheet (signed in)
links.look: Sign in, press I'm stuck twice and finish the problem. On the class sheet the row reads as before (hint, model): the words and tags are unchanged.
links.notLive: Needs a Google sign-in and the class sheet; the record itself is checked by the parity tests.

items.name: Add: what the addition did (Build D-2, Part 1)
items.about: An addition that doesn't cancel lights the two numbers added and their (bigger) sum, and says so in the student's numbers; a partial one names both numbers; only real opposites are crossed off.

links.label: +8 added to x + 8
links.look: Add 8, Go: the two 8s and the big 16 are lit; “+8 + +8 did not eliminate the term. Let’s try again.” The 8s are not crossed off.

links.label: Partly cancelled
links.look: Add −5, Go: “+8 was only partially canceled by the −5 you added. What value instead of −5 would have completely canceled the +8?” and “still here” under the 3.

links.label: Real opposites
links.look: Add −8, Go: the +8 and −8 are crossed off.

items.name: The light design (Build D, Part 1)
items.about: No banner: every message is a pop-up; one green button right of x =; the narrow panel with its small lights; help tucked in the corner; no number pad on a keyboard.

links.label: Add · Level 1 · x + 8 = 11
links.look: A small “Find the value of x.” goes at your first action. The header fades after 3 seconds (move to the top to bring it back). Type straight from the keyboard: no pad.

links.label: The one green button
links.look: Hover near Add: the preview starts faintly, then fully on the icon. Click Add, type −8: the button says Go. Enter: it says Next. Enter, type −12: Check, then Next, then Next problem. Always the same place.

links.label: An error below the work
links.look: Add 8 and Enter: the page dims, +16 is lit with “got bigger” under it, the message is below the work and an arrow hops at Undo.

links.label: Partly cancelled
links.look: Add −5: “still here” sits under the +3, not on it.

links.label: The move after a correct guess
links.look: Type −12, Enter four times, then Next problem: everything greys except the problem and the moves, with “Your mental math is very strong.” Hover Add: its preview is lit too. Next or a move brings everything back.

links.label: Help in the corner
links.look: Wait 10 seconds: I’m stuck flashes gently. Teach me appears (and flashes) only after a second error: try Add 8, Undo, Add 8.

links.label: Divide it in the light design
links.look: The same frame: the narrow panel (Multiply is the live move), x = with the green button, help in the corner, the counters on the right when you ask for help.

items.name: Checking a value side by side (Build D, Part 2)
items.about: Check greys the page except the original equation and the space to its right; drag your value into x, and the check is written beside the equation, one step a Next.

links.label: A right answer
links.look: Add −8, Enter, Enter, type 3, Check: drag the 3 into x (or tap x): (3) + 8 = 11 appears on the right; Next, Next: Balanced.

links.label: The opposite (−8)
links.look: Type −8 and Check, drag it into x, Next, Next: “−8 is an important number…”. Undo: the hint lights Add with −8 already in its blank.

links.label: Added sizes (19)
links.look: Add −8, Enter, Enter, type 19, Check, drag, Next, Next: “When x = 19, the equation is not balanced.” Undo: 11 − 8: party or battle? right above the numbers.

links.label: Any other wrong value
links.look: Type 4, Check, drag, Next, Next: “When x = 4, the equation is not balanced.” Undo: the usual reminder at the +8.

links.label: Divide it
links.look: Type 4, Check, drag the 4 into the x of 5x: 5 × 4 = −15 is written on the right, then 20 = −15, Not balanced.

items.name: Dragging terms: see where it lands (Build D, Part 3)
items.about: While you drag a term, the equation it would make shows in grey right under it; the token is green while positive and turns red with its new sign across the line; the line shows only while dragging.

links.label: Drag a number
links.look: Drag the + 8: before x the grey row shows 8 + x; over the line it turns red (− 8) and the grey row shows x = −8 + 11 or x = 11 − 8, depending on where you hold it.

links.label: x stays
links.look: Drag x across the line: “x is already on the left side of the equation…”, no dimming.

links.label: Combine
links.look: Drag − 3 across, then drop the 3 on the −1: the two are lit with Combine over them, the rest greys, a box under them; type 2 and press the green Combine. A wrong sum is an error with Undo.

links.label: Drill: finish with Flip and Multiply
links.look: At −2x = 2 a hint lights Flip everything; then Multiply, type 2 (1 over 2), Go: x = −1.

items.name: Divide it: the fraction blank and the fraction cycle (Build D, Part 4)
items.about: The fraction buttons are gone: the move is a blank you type a fraction into, with the same hover preview as Add; a fraction that doesn't split leads to the boxes and a list of fractions, the tried ones crossed off.

links.label: 5x = −15
links.look: Hover the move: ▢(5x) = ▢(−15) in grey. Click it, type 1/2, Go: the “can't split” box. Undo: the five boxes bracketed, “We want only one of the five x boxes.”, ½ crossed off. Pick ⅓: the same again, ½ and ⅓ crossed off. Pick ⅕: it applies, 1 of the 5 boxes is kept in the picture, and the green button says Next.

items.name: Scaffolds in the light design (Build D, Part 5)
items.about: Party or Battle floats right at the numbers or counters with the rest greyed; a battle's pairs stay crossed off; Teach me fills the Add blank and says Do it; the seesaw's tray adds a piece every tap; numbers past 12 get Count it's big-number walk.

links.label: Teach me
links.look: Make two errors (Add 8, Undo, Add 8, Undo) so Teach me appears, then press it: “To cancel the +8 we add its opposite, −8, to both sides”, −8 already in the blank, the green button says Do it. Then party or battle at −4 − 8; it never writes −12.

links.label: Party or Battle on the seesaw
links.look: I’m stuck twice (the seesaw), Add −8 to the left and to the right, Go: the question floats at the two groups, the rest greyed. Battle: the pairs stay on the balance, crossed off, until Next.

links.label: The tray adds a piece every tap
links.look: I’m stuck twice, pick +, then tap the left side three times: three counters, and + stays picked.

links.label: Numbers past 12
links.look: Add 13, Enter, Enter, then I’m stuck: party or battle; again: Add or Subtract, then the sign, beside the numbers. Then type x yourself.

links.label: Counters crossed off at x alone
links.look: Add −8, Enter, Enter, I’m stuck, Battle, I’m stuck: draw the counters, Check, tap pairs: crossed-off counters stay, slashed.

items.name: The narrow panel (was lights round 2)
items.about: Kept (Build D): the narrow panel with its small round lights is the only panel on Add to both sides and Divide it.

links.label: Narrow panel · x − 3 = −1
links.look: Hover a dot: it opens into its goal. The dashed line only shows while you drag a term.

items.name: Grab the terms (was lights round 2)
items.about: Kept (Build D): drag a number across the line, onto another number to combine, or along its side to reorder; tap a minus to see it as a negative.

links.label: Drag across, combine, minus
links.look: Drag “− 3” over the line, drop, then drop the 3 onto the −1, type 2 and press the green Combine.

links.label: Reorder, and x can’t cross
links.look: Drag “+ 8” before x: 8 + x = 11 in place. Drag x across: “That moves x. Try the number.”

items.name: The Distribute drill
items.about: Kept (Build D): two drill problems solved only by grabbing terms. It has no level button; this link is the way in.

links.label: Drill: 5 − 2(x + 2) = 3
links.look: Dragging the 2 is refused until you tap its minus; then two labelled blanks, −2 and −4, and on to x = −1.

items.name: Errors pop up next to the mistake (spotlight)
items.about: A move that makes things worse dims the page, lights up what went wrong, and only Undo goes on; after Undo a hint pops up at the number to work on.

links.label: A move the wrong way
links.look: On x + 8 = −4, Add 8 and Enter: the page dims, +16 is lit with “got bigger”, the message sits beside it and Undo pulses. Press Undo (or Enter): a hint at the +8 with Got it.

links.label: Partly cancelled
links.look: Add −5 and Enter: the +3 still next to x is lit, “still here”.

links.label: A wrong guess
links.look: Type 4 and Check, click through: the “Not balanced” line is lit; Undo takes the guess back, then the hint.

links.label: A wrong value
links.look: Add −8, Enter, Enter, then type 19 and Check, click through: x = is lit, “check this”; Undo closes it and says to work out x.

links.label: Divide: a fraction that doesn’t split
links.look: Type 1/2 in the move’s blank and Go: the failed row is lit, “doesn’t split”; after Undo the boxes and the list of fractions.

items.name: Help when x is alone: party or battle, then counters
items.about: At x = 11 + −8, I’m stuck asks “party or battle?” right at the two numbers, then says “Now type x.”; asked again, Count it’s counters appear in a small tray above the numbers.

links.label: x = 11 + −8
links.look: Add −8, Enter, Enter, then I’m stuck: pick Battle (a wrong pick gets a nudge), then I’m stuck again: draw 11 + counters and 8 − counters, Check, cancel the pairs, count, type 3. The app never writes 3.

links.label: Teach me starts at the counters
links.look: Add −8, Enter, Enter, then Teach me: the counters tray opens straight away, with its own Party or Battle step.

items.name: Add to both sides: preview on hover, fill the blank
items.about: Every level now plays this way: hover Add to see the move on the equation, type the amount in the box in that row, then press the green Next.

links.label: Level 1 · x + 8 = 11
links.look: No Guess x / Use a move buttons: the line just says “Find x.”, and both Add and x = work at once.

links.label: Level 3 · x + 8 = −4
links.look: The same screen on the mixed level (it used to be the old screen).

links.label: Level 5 · bigger
links.look: The same screen on the last level.

items.name: Trade places when x is on the right
items.about: From Level 4, when x is on the right, the line asks you to trade places first; Add waits until you do.

links.label: Level 4 · −2 = x + −6
links.look: Click Add first: it says to trade places. Click the Trade places move (it pulses): the sides swap, then Add works.

items.name: The move after a correct guess
items.about: Guess right and the next problem must be shown with a move: the move has a steady ring and x = stays grey until you make one.

links.label: Guess, then the next problem
links.look: Type −12 and Check, click through, then Next problem: Add has a ring, x = is grey with “Make one move first.”, until a good move and Next.

items.name: Divide it: no choice
items.about: Divide it has no Guess x / Use a move either: the fraction move and x = are both live from the start.

links.label: Divide it · Level 2 · 5x = −15
links.look: The line says “Find x.”; you can type a guess or pick Take a fraction straight away.

items.name: Level 1 is problems; the walkthrough is “See why it works”
items.about: Add to both sides and Divide it open on real problems; the numbers-only walkthrough is a small button on the card.

links.label: Home screen, as a brand-new student
links.look: Hover Solve it: both cards start at Level 1 with a “See why it works” button by the dots. Open it, reload: you land on the home screen.

links.label: Add to both sides · See why it works
links.look: The header says “See why it works”: the balance walkthrough.

links.label: Divide it · See why it works
links.look: The header says “See why it works”: the numbers-only walkthrough.

items.name: Help that reads the equation on screen (Build A)
items.about: I'm stuck now uses the numbers on screen, says Undo first after a bad move, and never writes the answer.

links.label: Partly cancelled: Undo first
links.look: On x + 8 = −4 add −5 (Enter), then I’m stuck: it names the +3 that’s left and says to press Undo first.

links.label: Divide it: a fraction that doesn’t split
links.look: On 5x = −15 type 1/2 in the move’s blank and Go (it fails), then I’m stuck: it says to press Undo first.
